highlights.headline: Long-form rose from 44% to 67% of the videos YouTube surfaces for the topic; Shorts went from 33% to 12%
highlights.detail: Median video length moved from 5.5 min to 13.4 min. Within 2026 YTD, longer videos also earn more reach relative to videos of the same age (Spearman ρ duration × relative velocity = 0.30, vs 0.04 in 2025 YTD).
highlights.evidence: Long-form share q < 0.001 · Shorts share q < 0.001 · median length q < 0.001 (Benjamini-Hochberg, 24 tests)

highlights.headline: Engagement ratio +15% YoY, driven by Shorts (+70%) while long-form moved −11%
highlights.detail: The link between length and engagement reversed: Spearman ρ duration × engagement went from +0.36 to −0.22. Comment rate moved +23% (q = 0.014). Long-form now wins reach; short videos win interaction per view.
highlights.evidence: Overall 95% CI [−1%, +32%] · q = 0.033 · Shorts n = 23 this year, q = 0.002 · long-form q = 0.526

highlights.headline: 32% of 2025 YTD videos carried coordinated brand-promotion comments, vs 4% in 2026 YTD
highlights.detail: 199 comments promoting 5 products were removed before scoring sentiment. On the remaining organic comments, the negative share went from 8.6% to 9.0%: no significant change.
highlights.evidence: Videos with promo comments: two-proportion z-test q < 0.001 · organic negative share q = 0.859. Older videos had more time to collect spam.

recommendations.title: Build for reach with long-form, for interaction with Shorts
recommendations.body: Across both windows the 20–40m band earns the most reach relative to videos of the same age (median 1.82× the typical video), and in 2026 YTD the duration–reach correlation rose to 0.30. Shorts are now a minority of what surfaces but carry a higher engagement ratio (3.16% vs 2.60% for long-form, on only 23 Shorts): use them to start conversations, not to win discovery.

recommendations.title: Follow the vocabulary: claude, business
recommendations.body: Title terms gaining weight: “claude”, “business”, “claude code”. Fading: “n8n”, “aiagent”. “claude”, “claude code”, “n8n” move the same way in what viewers write in comments, which makes it a demand signal and not only a creator trend.

recommendations.title: Audit comment sections before reading sentiment
recommendations.body: 32% of last year's videos in this niche carried coordinated brand-promotion comments. Positive-sounding comment sections can be bought: require organic-engagement reporting (with spam and creator comments removed) before using comment sentiment as a placement KPI.

recommendations.title: Price reach on channel size, judge quality on engagement
recommendations.body: Channel size is the most stable predictor of reach in both years (Spearman ρ subscribers × relative velocity = 0.36 → 0.38). Use it to set CPM expectations. The link between channel size and engagement flipped sign (ρ = +0.30 → −0.20): in the current window larger channels get less interaction per view. Compare creators on engagement only within the same subscriber tier.

recommendations.title: Watch Tools & Launches as an early friction signal
recommendations.body: Negative organic comments in Tools & Launches went from 9.4% to 15.2% (q = 0.082). Not significant after correcting for multiple tests: monitor it, but don't act on it yet.
